title: Know Your Robot Arcade
intro: Six rounds on ARIA's parts and systems. Get them right first try to earn ⭐⭐⭐!

rounds.prompt: Which system does the controller board belong to?
rounds.explain: The controller reads the sensors and decides what to do. That is the THINK step, built out of hardware.

rounds.prompt: Match each system to the job only it does.

pairs.right: Holds every other part in place

rounds.explain: Six systems, one job each. Senses, Brain and Movement are the loop itself. Power and Frame are what make the loop possible.

rounds.prompt: Why are ARIA's line sensors mounted underneath the chassis?
options: They have to see the floor to tell a dark line from a light surface
There was not room on the deck
To keep them safe from knocks
rounds.explain: Position follows job. Their only question is about the floor beneath the robot, so that is where they point.

rounds.prompt: In an exploded view, ARIA's wheels move straight out sideways. Why?
options: Sideways is the direction you would really slide them off the motor shafts
It just looks better that way
rounds.explain: An exploded view moves each part the way it really comes off, which means it doubles as an assembly guide.

rounds.prompt: Your robot is completely dead, with no LED and no movement. Which system do you check first?
rounds.explain: A flat battery looks exactly like a broken brain from the outside. Power is the quickest thing to rule out.

rounds.prompt: ARIA has a ball at the front instead of a third wheel. What is it for?
options: It rolls in any direction, so it holds the front up without fighting the driven wheels
rounds.explain: Two wheels can drive and steer, but they cannot balance the robot on their own. The caster ball is the third point of the triangle.
